name: Absolute Path Traversal
principle: The product constructs a pathname from external input but does not reject absolute path forms. Absolute paths can escape the intended restricted directory and access, overwrite, or corrupt unexpected files.
detection_signals: Java FileInputStream(request.getParameter(...)), new File(userInput), Paths.get(userInput), or Files.readAllBytes(Paths.get(userInput))
C fopen(userInput,...), open(userInput,...), unlink(userInput), remove(userInput), or rename(userInput,...) with argv/env/request input
C++ std::ifstream(userInput), std::ofstream(userInput), std::filesystem::path(userInput), or std::filesystem::remove(userInput) with external input
base path joined with user input using new File(base,userInput), base.resolve(userInput), operator/(base,userPath), or string concatenation without rejecting isAbsolute()
validation blocks only "../" or "..\\" and lacks checks for leading "/", leading "\\", drive prefix "C:", or UNC prefix "\\\\"
normalize(), canonicalize(), realpath(), getCanonicalPath(), or toRealPath() used without checking canonical target starts under canonical base
download/upload/delete/open endpoint accepts a raw path or filename parameter that may include directory separators
negative_signals: raw input is mapped through a server-side allowlist ID to a fixed filename before any file API call
code rejects Path.isAbsolute(), File.isAbsolute(), std::filesystem::path::is_absolute(), leading '/', leading '\\', drive-letter prefixes, and UNC prefixes
candidate path is canonicalized with realpath(), File.getCanonicalPath(), or Path.toRealPath() and verified as a child of the canonical base directory
only basename is used via Paths.get(input).getFileName() or equivalent plus strict allowlist for characters, length, and extension
file path argument is a compile-time constant or trusted internal configuration, not request/argv/env/user controlled
false_defense_traps: blocking only "../" does not block "/etc/passwd", "C:\\Windows\\...", or "\\\\server\\share"
joining base and user path can be bypassed when an absolute user path overrides or escapes the base
startsWith(base) before canonicalization is bypassable by encoding, symlinks, or normalization
filtering only '/' misses Windows '\\', drive-letter paths, and UNC paths
single-pass removal of dangerous substrings can create a new dangerous path after transformation
verification_focus: Can external input reach a file sink as an absolute pathname outside the intended base directory?

consequence_chains.trigger: absolute path used in a read sink
consequence_chains.consequence: read arbitrary files and expose sensitive data

consequence_chains.trigger: absolute path used in an upload or write sink with attacker-controlled content
consequence_chains.consequence: create or overwrite executable files and enable code execution

consequence_chains.trigger: canonical check permits a path through a symbolic link outside the base
consequence_chains.consequence: escape directory restriction and access unintended files

patch_principle: Use accept-known-good validation for filename characters, length, and extension.
Reject absolute paths before resolving or opening user-supplied path text.
Decode and canonicalize once, then verify the canonical target is under the canonical base directory.
Prefer server-side ID-to-file mapping instead of accepting raw path strings.
Use safe relative-path APIs anchored to a trusted directory where available.

minimal_examples.safe: Path p = base.resolve(name).normalize(); if (Paths.get(name).isAbsolute() || !p.startsWith(base)) throw new SecurityException();
